decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) an abrupt multi-axis shift near index 490–500 with persistent N elevation and E/U drop, and (2) a large, complex offset beginning near index 690 involving a sharp E spike and sustained N/U changes without full reversal in the observed window.

regions.observation: N/E/U show a multi-sample shift around index ~490–500: N jumps from ~1 to ~2.8, E drops sharply from ~-1.6 to ~-2.8, U falls from ~0.8 to ~-0.4; the change is abrupt over 2–3 samples and not clearly reversed in the window, though later samples (e.g., index 510 onward) show some recovery in E and U but N remains elevated.

A large, sustained offset appears starting near index 690: N rises abruptly from ~2–3 to ~5–6, E shifts from ~-2 to ~-1 to ~+9 (peaking at index 695), and U drops from ~-1 to ~-7 then recovers partially; the event spans ~10 samples with complex cross-axis behavior—E shows a sharp spike while N and U shift more gradually, suggesting superposed motion or instrument anomaly; no clear return within the window.
